jobs.description: At Dow, we believe in putting people first and we’re passionate about delivering integrity, respect and safety to our customers, our employees and the planet. Develops maintenance procedures based on Most Effective Technology (MET). Enters quality complaints into the QSPP system. Participates in developing the equipment maintenance strategy by providing technical and historical information. Participates in developing the maintenance budget to support the maintenance strategy. Serves as a technical resource to the planner on work packages. During development of turnaround work, provides input on scope of work. Do you want to help millions of customers protect their cloud workloads? The AWS security services team is building the next generation of security monitoring products that give customers a unified view of threats, risks, and compliance across multiple cloud environments. As a Software Development Engineer II on this team, you will design and build integrations that connect internal and external services, ingest infrastructure metadata and security findings at scale, and solve complex problems around data correctness and cross-provider modeling differences. With the rapid expansion of AI reshaping how customers manage security, there has never been a more compelling time to join — our team is investing heavily in delivering the right information, at the right time, with the right context so customers can understand risk and prioritize remediation faster.

Key job responsibilities
- Design and build service integrations using industry-standard authentication protocols such as OAuth and OpenID Connect (OIDC) to establish secure connectivity with internal and external platforms.
- Develop data ingestion pipelines that collect infrastructure metadata, context, and security findings across multiple cloud providers, solving challenges around scale, data correctness, and cross-provider modeling differences.
- Own requirements end-to-end by driving discussions with product, UX, console, and partner engineering teams to gather and clarify requirements, then translate them into designs, prototypes, and production-ready software.
- Mentor peers and junior engineers through thoughtful code reviews and design feedback, championing software quality best practices across the team.
- Own operational health for the services you build maintain alarms, dashboards, and runbooks, participate in on-call rotations, and ensure root causes of operational issues are permanently resolved.

A day in the life
You will operate with a high degree of independence on a roadmap-driven team. Some weeks you will be heads-down writing and testing code for a new integration; other weeks you will pair with product managers or partner engineers to prototype a solution and align on requirements. You will regularly review teammates' designs and code, sharing your perspective to raise the quality bar. When operational issues arise, you will dig into metrics and logs to find permanent fixes rather than temporary workarounds.

About the team
Our team within AWS builds customer-facing security products that help organizations measure and manage their security posture across AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud Platform (GCP). We are a growing group with a broad mix of experience levels, and we prioritize mentorship — expect thorough yet supportive code reviews and projects designed to stretch your skills. Our mission over the coming years is to expand our monitoring capabilities so customers receive actionable, contextualized security insights in a single pane of glass that let them remediate risks faster and with greater confidence.

This position works out of our Westfield, IN, location in the Structural Heart division (SH).

· Able to train to achieve standard work and assembly time and rotate on 4-5 stations to relieve WIP as directed.

· Utilize 5S tools to improve station layout

Requires comprehensive knowledge of various tools/equipment/fixtures for various product types.

About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the Role

Anthropic's People Legal team is looking for a Lead Employment Counsel to build the legal foundation for our growing workforce across Asia-Pacific. You'll partner closely with our People team and business leaders to design and run employment programs in the region that help our people do their best work.

This role pairs deep employment law expertise with pragmatism and creativity. You'll build structures that manage legal risk across several APAC countries today and that will hold up as our presence in the region scales. You'll also help colleagues around the world understand how local requirements shape the way we hire, manage, and support people in APAC.

Key responsibilities

•

Serve as the primary employment lawyer for Anthropic's APAC region, partnering with People and business leaders across People programs, policies and day-to-day issues

•

Build and maintain the legal infrastructure for new and existing APAC jurisdictions, including Japan, South Korea, Australia, Singapore and India

•

Advise on market entry and workforce structuring, including acquisitions, employer of record arrangements, contractor classification, and headcount thresholds that trigger local obligations

•

Partner with Compensation, Benefits, and Equity teams so that global programs are compliant and scalable

•

Guide employee relations matters, including workplace investigations, in line with local law and practice

•

Develop and manage strategy on employment disputes across the region, from pre-litigation claims through tribunal and court proceedings, in partnership with outside counsel

•

Track legislative and regulatory developments across the region, including employee data privacy and emerging rules on AI in employment, and turn them into practical guidance

•

Develop scalable templates, playbooks, and training that enable stakeholders to operate compliantly

Minimum qualifications

•

Hold a law degree (JD, LLB, or equivalent) and meet the local licensing requirements to work as in-house counsel where you'll be based

•

Have deep subject-matter expertise on employment law across multiple APAC countries

•

Write clearly and concisely, and can provide actionable guidance to non-lawyers

•

Balance legal risk with business practicality, and work collaboratively with legal and business cross-functional partners

•

Work effectively with colleagues and stakeholders across multiple time zones

Preferred qualifications

•

At least 12+ years of relevant employment legal experience across law firms and in-house, with demonstrated experience supporting companies through rapid growth

•

Experience advising People and business teams on the practical application of employment laws in Japan, South Korea, India, Australia, and Singapore

•

Creative and pragmatic in your approach to developing legal solutions to business problems

•

Working knowledge of employee data privacy requirements across the region

Role-specific policy: For this role, we expect all staff to be able to work from our Sydney office at least 3 days a week, though we encourage you to apply even if you might need some flexibility for an interim period of time.

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. As an early member of our Safeguards Data Science and Analytics team, you will play an instrumental role in our company’s mission of building safe and beneficial artificial intelligence by building and scaling a data driven culture from the ground up. You will work closely with product, engineering, policy & enforcement to define and measure key company success metrics, analyze user behavior to identify new enforcement opportunities and build a culture of developing and testing hypotheses through experimentation. You’ve worked in cultures of excellence in the past, and are eager to apply that experience to building robust and scalable systems and processes as our company goes through a phase of rapid growth.

• Highly effective written communication and presentation skills.
• A passion for the company's mission of building helpful, honest, and harmless AI.

Preferred qualifications

We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.
